via.name: Pakihi stream

evidence: The cycling direction is one-way only, starting from Motu Road.
For cyclists, the start of the Pakihi Track is from the Mōtū Road, at close to 600 m altitude.
The top half of the track is a steady descent, dropping over 400 m to the Pakihi Hut.
Around 1 km after the hut you reach the Pakihi stream suspension bridge, a spectacular 32-m structure that spans a pretty gorge.
At the end of the track, there is a shelter, car park and toilet.
Cycling is one-way from Mōtū Road to Pakihi Road.

ways.label: Walk from the Pakihi road end up and back

start.name: Pakihi road end
start.quote: Hunters, walkers and trail runners often start from the Pakihi road end, going up and back

via.name: Pakihi stream
via.quote: following the Pakihi stream all the way

evidence: For walking or running, you can go both ways, with most doing an out-and-back trip.
Hunters, walkers and trail runners often start from the Pakihi road end, going up and back.
A popular walk is from the Pakihi road to the Mōtū Road junction, then turn around and head to Pakihi Hut for the night.

not_on_route.name: Mōtū Road Trail
not_on_route.quote: Mōtū Road Trail is a good alternative

doubts: The page is written mainly for cyclists (one-way Mōtū Road to Pakihi Road); for walkers it says most do an out-and-back from the Pakihi road end, recorded as W2. Pakihi Hut is the section boundary in the headings, but the text says 'two side-tracks down to the Pakihi Hut and the stream', so the hut may sit just off the main track. The popular walkers' version (to Mōtū Road junction then back to the hut overnight, 30 km + 10 km) has no single stated time for W2.
